question: Does a body-grounded signal (foot slip, actuator saturation, work, joint-limit proximity, undesired contact) satisfy what a difficulty gate needs -- anchored at fixed difficulty, responsive to difficulty at fixed competence, and responsive to the actuator with the right sign -- better than the latent gap, return or survival?
caveats: training telemetry is a population mean per iteration over all 1,024 environments, so it mixes strata in stratified arms and mixes episodes at every stage of survival

evaluator batch diagnostics include auto-reset environments after their scored episode terminates (receipt: not_yet_verified), so per-cell physical means are contaminated in the same way the tracking-error metrics are; the difficulty-response correlations are reported with that contamination, not corrected for it
